description: Regulator-side 'jobs/hiring' coverage (NBU and FGVFO own vacancies, competitive selections for regulator staff) is not yet sourced.
bank.gov.ua — the core domain for this cell — is bot-defended for plain HTTP fetchers (403 observed once).
Few pointer/archive sources identified (no confirmed RSS endpoints, no confirmed sitemap or API endpoint for NBU news, no web-archive strategy).
Payment-institution leadership (non-bank PSPs licensed under the Law on Payment Services) is thinly covered relative to banks; no person-level authoritative source found.
English-language coverage of payment-provider licensing decisions is sparse; most substantive detail exists only in Ukrainian.

Executive-search / headhunting firms engaged by MoF and by the banks' supervisory boards (the Oschadbank CEO competition explicitly used international recruiters, and MoF ran a tender for an executive-search company for Ukreximbank) were not identified by name.

IFI/donor-side sources (EBRD, IFC, EU, IMF structural benchmarks on SOE corporate governance) were not scouted, although IFIs nominate or vet independent board members and IMF programme documents set dated conditionality on state-bank governance.
Professional-network and first-person channels (LinkedIn profiles of state-bank executives, their public posts announcing moves) were not covered.

Annual reports, corporate-governance reports and audited financial statements of the five banks — which contain the authoritative year-end board rosters, committee composition, attendance and organisational charts — were not systematically located beyond one Ukrgasbank org-structure PDF.
Russian-language variants of the search terms (наблюдательный совет, председатель правления) were only incidentally encountered via kurs.com.ua and RBC's ru edition, not deliberately queried.

Archival/backfill sources for reconstructing multi-year board rotation history (web.archive.org snapshots of bank governance pages, the full Kyiv Independent SOE Weekly back-catalogue of 150+ issues) were identified but not enumerated.

Card-scheme adjacent and other foreign-parent employers in Ukraine were not covered in this pass: BNP Paribas (Ukrsibbank), Credit Agricole Ukraine, ProCredit Holding, Pravex/Intesa Sanpaolo, and UnionPay/Diners.
Professional-network profile changes (the most timely signal for country-manager and regional-lead moves) were not assessed as a source channel.
Card-scheme careers portals (Visa, Mastercard) were not located in this pass, leaving the 'jobs/hiring' topic for schemes covered only for Western Union and EBRD.
Ukrainian-language payments trade press (e.g. PaySpace Magazine/psm7, Mind.ua, Ekonomichna Pravda) was only partially sampled; only Forbes.ua, Minfin, FinClub and Mind surfaced.

Several candidate index URLs (Visa Ukraine press-release index, Mastercard EEMEA press-release index, IFC pressroom, EBRD news index, RBI press-release index) were inferred from individual article URLs rather than confirmed as live listing pages.
EBRD/IFC equity stakes in Ukrainian banks and the specific nominee directors they have placed were not enumerated.

Only three EDRPOU codes were confirmed in this run (NBU 00032106, Oschadbank 00032129, Ukreximbank 00032112, plus branch 09305480). PrivatBank, Ukrgasbank, Sense Bank, the State Treasury, SE Diia and the Deposit Guarantee Fund codes are not yet mapped.
No validated CPV code set was assembled for banking/payments IT, core banking, HR services and management consultancy.
State banks run 'відбір комерційних пропозицій' outside Prozorro for law-exempt procurements; only Ukreximbank's channel was located.
Prozorro operates through accredited eMall brokers (Zakupki.prom.ua, E-Tender, SmartTender, gov.auction and others); only one aggregator and one auction domain were incidentally observed.
USAID-successor programmes, GIZ, EU4Digital/EU4Business, EIB and Swiss/Nordic bilateral procurement for Ukrainian financial-sector TA were not covered.
spending.gov.ua was identified but its filtering/open-data export capabilities for a specific bank counterparty were not tested.
TAS-Link (TASK Bank group) processing centre was named in market overviews but no corporate site or news feed was located for it in this pass.
Vendor and integrator LinkedIn company pages (BPC, OpenWay, CS, UPC, SoftServe) were not systematically enumerated, yet they are where partner-hire and client-win posts appear fastest.
Local-language coverage of the multinational vendors (Temenos, Oracle FS, OpenWay, BPC) was thin — Ukrainian queries mainly retrieved domestic vendors.
Ukrainian IT-vendor job aggregators beyond DOU (djinni.co, work.ua, robota.ua) were not covered, and no per-bank in-house IT hiring feed was captured.
Several vendor root domains (bpcbt.com, ciklum.com, infopulse.com, profix.com.ua) were recorded from search context without confirming the exact newsroom/case-study paths.
Closed/private Facebook groups and closed Telegram chats for Ukrainian finance practitioners are invisible to both search engines and logged-out access.

Only large banks' LinkedIn company pages were enumerated (Raiffeisen, monobank, PrivatBank, OTP, FUIB). Second-tier banks (Oschadbank, Ukrgasbank, Ukrsibbank, Credit Agricole UA, A-Bank, Sense Bank, Pivdennyi, Concord, Alliance, Industrialbank) and payment/fintech firms (NovaPay, EasyPay, Portmone, Fondy, Wise-adjacent players) are not yet mapped in this cell.
No named-individual watchlist yet exists (payments heads, CIOs, CDTOs, retail heads), which is the unit at which this cell's signals actually occur.

The richest self-announcement text on LinkedIn is English, while the richest community discussion is Ukrainian on Telegram/Facebook; a single-language monitoring rule will miss half the signal. Russian-language posting still occurs among older banking cohorts but was out of the declared language scope (uk, en).
This cell produces unverified weak signals by design, but no corroboration path is defined against authoritative registers (NBU management approvals, YouControl/Opendatabot officer changes).
Telegram channel handles were discovered only via third-party listicles; no systematic enumeration (e.g. via a Telegram directory or the FinAwards nominee list in full) was completed.

Conference and award sites routinely delete or overwrite prior-edition speaker pages (kmbs, uafin.tech and the banksinfo.kiev.ua subdomains all show single-edition front pages). Without an archive, year-over-year title diffing — the core value of this cell — is impossible.

For most candidates the presence and format of a speaker/jury roster is inferred from event descriptions and press coverage rather than from a fetched roster page; only the EMA conferences index was actually fetched, and it carried no speaker data.
All discovered events are Kyiv-centred. No western-Ukraine (Lviv) or relocated-diaspora banking/fintech event series was identified, despite wartime relocation of financial operations.

Awards and headline forums over-represent CEOs and board chairs. Middle-management layers most relevant to hiring signal — heads of risk, compliance/AML, cards & acquiring, IT — are visible mainly through training-centre and niche-track agendas, which were only lightly probed.

Speaker announcements for these events are frequently published first on LinkedIn, Facebook and Instagram (UAFIC's Instagram appeared in results) rather than on the event website, and often carry the fullest title detail.
Russian-language variants of the same sites (nabu.ua/ru, minfin.com.ua/ru) exist and sometimes carry content the Ukrainian tree lacks, but ru was outside the declared language scope for this run.

Exact deep-link paths for Держстат labour-statistics tables filtered to KVED section K, and for the NBU supervisory statistics files containing staff headcount, were not pinned down within this pass; only the portal roots and example artefacts are recorded.

Ukrainian HR professional communities and HR-media (e.g. HR-associations, HR conferences, HR-focused media) were not systematically enumerated; no Ukrainian HR-professional body was confirmed in this pass.

Relocation and diaspora-employment angle (UA bank staff working from Poland/Germany, remote hubs, return intentions) is not yet covered by any source in this slice beyond generic KSE migration research.

The most decision-useful comp data (EBA full salary survey, recruiter benchmarks, FinClub full texts, Opendatabot API) sits behind paid or membership access, and job-board terms of service may restrict automated collection.
Almost all substantive workforce material for UA financial services exists only in Ukrainian; English coverage is thin and second-hand (Interfax-Ukraine, occasional Forbes/NV English items).
No first-party newsroom confirmed for àбанк / А-Банк, and Sense Bank's newsroom path is unconfirmed. Two of the cell's actors therefore lack a verified direct source.

This pass did not cover LinkedIn company pages, Facebook pages or Telegram channels for the cell's banks. For Ukrainian banks — and especially for monobank, whose founders communicate primarily via Telegram — social channels frequently break appointment and reorganisation news before the corporate site, and executives announce their own moves on LinkedIn before any employer release.

Only one structured organisational-structure disclosure was located (the OTP Bank shareholder-stakeholder PDF, dated 1 July 2026). UA transparency rules appear to impose a comparable obligation sector-wide, so equivalent artefacts almost certainly exist for PUMB, Raiffeisen, Credit Agricole, ProCredit and Universal Bank but were not located in this pass.

Group-level investor-relations channels of the foreign parents were not scouted: RBI (Raiffeisen Bank International, Vienna), OTP Group (Budapest), Crédit Agricole SA (Paris), ProCredit Holding AG (Frankfurt). Parents often announce or disclose subsidiary CEO changes and country-level restructuring in IR releases and annual reports before or instead of the local subsidiary.

Russian-language (ru) variants of these bank sites still exist (e.g. raiffeisen.ua/ru/press/news) and hold historical archives, but ru is outside the declared run languages (uk, en). Older leadership-move records may only be retrievable in ru.

No web-archive strategy was established. Bank newsrooms prune old items and board roster pages are overwritten in place, so departures are erased rather than recorded. Confidence in historical leadership timelines therefore degrades sharply going backwards.
Professional-network sources (LinkedIn company/people pages, Djinni, and UA recruiter/HR-agency newsletters covering fintech) are entirely absent from this slice.

The actor map is incomplete: money-transfer operators and smaller licensed PSPs (e.g. IntelExpress, Welsend, Leo/Leogaming entities, TYME, Fondy's UA entity, Weld Money, Maxi/regional terminal networks) were not individually resolved to legal entity + EDRPOU.
Russian-language UA payment media and Telegram channels were not covered, although a material share of UA fintech insider newsflow (including personnel rumours) circulates in RU-language Telegram.

No court/enforcement or sanctions register sources were captured, though NBU enforcement (fines on EasyPay/City24) and professional-suitability rulings are a leading indicator of forced management change.
No URL in this slice was fetched or confirmed reachable; all entries are search-result-derived with stated confidence only.
LinkedIn (company pages and individual title changes) was not scouted in this pass, despite being the canonical place a Ukrainian fintech product lead announces a new role.

Adjacent card-issuing / payment challengers that compete for the same talent (NovaPay, Sense SuperApp of Alfa/Sense Bank, Concord-successor fintechs, Wise/Payoneer-style local issuers) are outside the current actor list, yet appointments there (e.g. NovaPay's new CEO, Aug 2026) move people between the neobanks.

Founder channels other than Horokhovskyi's were not enumerated — no source pinned for Mykhailo Rohalskyi, the Dubilet brothers, or product leads (Instagram/Threads/Facebook), which the cell rationale says are primary.
Several access/legal assessments (DOU, Djinni, Facebook, Opendatabot/YouControl licensing) are hypotheses about robots.txt and ToS, not checked terms.
Russian-language coverage (still used by parts of the UA fintech press and by some founder posts) was not searched, per run scope uk/en.

No systematic list of UA banks and licensed payment institutions mapped to their career-page URLs and their employer-profile slugs on DOU/Djinni/robota.ua was assembled in this pass; only a handful (PrivatBank, mono, OTP Bank UA, Accordbank, Alfa/Sense, Platon) were confirmed.

Job boards show vacancies, not appointments. The 'leadership moves' topic is only weakly covered by this cell — LinkedIn (the natural source) is blocked, and boards rarely reveal who actually took a role.

Hiring-location-shift analysis assumes comparable board coverage across oblasts; wartime displacement, relocated head offices and closed branches distort this, and small-town coverage sits mainly with aggregators (Jooble) whose data quality is lower.

Run languages were uk and en only. A meaningful share of legacy UA vacancy text (especially aggregator mirrors and older postings) is still Russian-language ('эквайринг', 'платёжные системы', 'руководитель департамента').
For every commercial board in this cell, robots.txt and ToS were not inspected in this pass, and no rate-limit or bot-defence posture was tested.
Coverage found in this cell skews heavily to banks (and specifically to state banks and scandal-driven stories). Payments/fintech leadership moves are represented almost solely by PaySpace Magazine.

Media coverage reliably captures board-chair and supervisory-board level moves, but only sporadically captures C-1/C-2 changes (CIO, head of retail, head of cards/payments) which matter most for vendor-relevant intelligence.

Only tag archives (Ukrinform /tag-bank with 46+ pages, NV tag pages, dated LB.ua paths) offer confirmed deep pagination. Backfill depth for Forbes Ukraine, LIGA finance and finclub.net was not established.
No RSS/JSON feed or public API was confirmed for any outlet in this cell; all collection designs currently assume HTML scraping.

English-language coverage in this cell rests almost entirely on Interfax (both editions). Ukrainian-language coverage is broad, but no Ukrainian outlet's English edition was checked for whether it mirrors personnel items.
A large share of the 2026 items surfaced concern a single story cluster (Sens Bank / NABU / Midas investigation). Frequency-based signals built on this period would be distorted by one scandal.

Even specialist outlets skew to board-level (голова правління, наглядова рада). Genuine second-tier roles — CISO, CTO, head of retail, regional director, head of acquiring — appeared only sporadically (one HRD item on Forbes, NBU department directors on NV/FinClub).

Payments-side personnel coverage is materially thinner than banking-side. PaySpace and EMA are the only strong payments-specific channels found; non-bank PSPs, acquirers, processors and money-transfer operators have no dedicated personnel wire.
Trade-press appointment reports are announcements, not legal facts; NBU fit-and-proper approval can lag or fail (the Sens Bank board-chair competency procedure is a live example).
All sources found are Kyiv-centric national outlets; no regional business press covering branch-network restructuring or regional-director moves was identified in this cell.

Paywalls (Mind.ua long-form, Forbes.ua features, NV metered) and ad/JS-heavy delivery (psm7, minfin) will limit full-text capture; several small sites (finbalance) have uncertain uptime. No liveness or bot-defence testing was performed in this run.
Russian-language variants of these outlets (and RU-language Ukrainian financial media) were not searched in this run; some archival personnel records pre-2022 exist mainly in RU.
Statutory registers reliably expose the single legal signatory (керівник), but not the wider management board, C-level hires, or regular staff hiring — the bulk of A5 'jobs and hiring' interest.

The highest-value real-time capability — an event stream of ЄДР director changes filtered to banks and payment providers — sits behind commercial APIs (Opendatabot, VKURSI, YouControl), not behind a free public endpoint.
Refresh cadence of the data.gov.ua ЄДР bulk dump was not established in this pass, so the achievable detection latency of a director change via the free route is unknown.

No single register was found that jointly enumerates banks and all non-bank payment service providers with a common identifier; the bank register, the payment infrastructure register and the NSSMC licensee lists must be joined manually.
Person-name matching across Ukrainian originals and English transliterations of banking executives has no authoritative crosswalk; only OpenSanctions offers partial entity resolution.
UAFIC (fintechua.org) — one of the four associations named in the cell pointer — is client-side rendered and its board/member data were not retrievable in this pass.

Canonical index URLs for the full member directories of NABU and AUB, and for AUB's committee list, were inferred from site navigation rather than fetched. EMA's members page is the only member directory directly verified.

EMA's board is published at institution level (Mastercard, Visa, PrivatBank, Raiffeisen, Oschadbank, Sens Bank, UkrSibbank, PUMB, Universal Bank, Ukrgasbank, OTP Bank, VST Bank). Delegate names — the actual A5 signal — were not extracted.

A cross-association Coordination Council of professional financial-market participants (AUB + PFTS + Stock Market Lawyers Association + League of Insurance Organisations and others) was found but not scouted, and its current membership and leadership are unknown. NBU-adjacent consultative bodies (Громадська рада при НБУ, Рада з фінансової стабільності) were likewise only glimpsed.

No association covering payment-service providers / e-money issuers as a distinct segment (as opposed to EMA's bank-and-scheme membership) was identified, nor any open-banking or PSP industry body under Ukraine's new payment-services regime.
Association rosters are snapshots with no published change history; the associations' own sites overwrite governance pages on re-election, so prior compositions are lost.

English coverage in this cell is thin and skewed to the foreign-business chambers (AmCham, EBA, USUBC); the three Ukrainian banking associations publish governance data almost exclusively in uk (NABU also carries a ru locale).
